caption.text: Figure 8: Claude 3.7 accuracy improves consistently with larger thinking-token budgets across three benchmarks. Each panel plots mean accuracy (markers) and ±1 standard error (error bars) over multiple independent runs (5 for AIME 24, 3 for LCB and GPQA Diamond). The horizontal axes are logarithmic in the number of thinking tokens; the answer budget is 1 024 tokens for AIME 24 and 4 096 tokens for LCB and GPQA Diamond and is not counted in the thinking tokens budget. AIME 24: accuracy rises from a no-thinking baseline of 18.0% (red diamond) to 51.3% when the model is allowed 62 976 thinking tokens. LCB: performance climbs steadily from 60.5% to 70.4% at 28 672 thinking tokens. GPQA Diamond: accuracy increases from 60.1% without thinking to ≈ 76% at 12 288 tokens, after which the curve plateaus, illustrating diminishing returns beyond this budget.

figures.label: Figure 11

caption.text: Figure 11: Distilled reasoning models show deficits in generalization. All distilled reasoning models exhibit strong performance fluctuations on AIW Friends variations 1-6 Nezhurina et al. (2024), despite the variations not changing problem structure at all. This points to generalization deficits. The fluctuations affect to same extent SFT only (eg S1.1 32B, LIMO-32B) and SFT+RL (eg Light-R1-32B, QwQ 32B) reasoning models. Smaller scale models, eg OpenThinker3-7B, perform worse than larger scale ones, eg OpenThinker-32B, showing overall lower correct response rates. Larger scale 32B models, while having higher overall correct response rate, show strong fluctuations, e.g. OpenThinker-32B going from close to 1 on variations 2 and 3 down to close to 0 on variation 1. For reference, o1-preview and o3-mini are shown, which have much smaller fluctuations and higher overall correct response rates. Distilled models still do not possess robust zero-shot generalization on simple problems. Numbers in the legend are prompt IDs, see Nezhurina et al. (2024) and AIW repo

caption.text: Figure 12: Reasoning models outperform conventional LLMs. Albeit suffering from strong fluctuations, larger-scale distilled reasoning models set themselves apart from the conventional language models from which they were distilled. cross_object_system.visual_narrative: The visual sequence moves from headline scaling (Figure 1) to the six-stage curation interface (Figure 2), the selected 1.2M accounting flow (Figure 3), then appends stage ablations, full benchmark scaling, compute/length diagnostics, safety/generalization checks and prompt reproductions. Figures 5–7 and Tables 31–48 make the main-to-appendix link explicit.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every PDF caption begins with a bold title or finding phrase, then uses regular text for setup, comparison and caveats. Main figures are unusually explanatory (Figures 1, 5–8, 11–12), while prompt screenshots and Figure 3 are title-only. Tables often state the decision rule and point to full appendix tables.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Performance tables use a left condition/model/source column followed by grouped benchmark columns and domain row labels. Metadata tables use explicit units or ranges. Vertical rules separate model families or full-scale versus controlled groups; horizontal booktabs rules establish table hierarchy.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 names each curation decision; Tables 2–7 test those decisions in order; Figure 5 stacks selected winners; Figure 3 renders the final recipe; Figures 6–10 and Tables 8–30 test scaling, compute, transfer, safety and failure boundaries; Tables 31–48 preserve omitted candidate rows.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figure 1 points to Figure 6, Table 2 points to Tables 31–33, Tables 3–7 point to Tables 34–48, Figure 2 points to Appendix O prompt cards, and Figure 11 points to AIW references. The link is strong in captions, although held-out panels are not visually marked in Figure 6.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern-like paper text, bold caption lead-ins and compact chart/table text are consistent across main and appendix pages. The monospaced prompt/trace artifacts form a deliberate secondary type role; appendix long tables fall to approximately 6 pt and are the main legibility compromise.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Red/blue/green/purple/orange recur as model or pipeline identities in scaling charts, while gray dashed lines consistently denote Qwen baselines. Process and prompt objects use independent pastel/grayscale systems, so color semantics are local to each object rather than globally categorical.

most_reusable_patterns: Shared-baseline log-scale small multiples for showing recipe scaling across heterogeneous benchmarks.
Cumulative pipeline curves paired with one-factor ablation tables, preserving both narrative and causal isolation.
Horizontal prompt cards with monospaced text, exact placeholders and a direct downstream table link for reproducibility.
Variation-level grouped bars followed by horizontal distribution summaries for separating average utility from generalization instability.
Alluvial accounting for dataset retention and repeated-answer expansion, with explicit intermediate counts.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: concise cross-domain headline with shared log x-axis and Qwen reference.
Figure 5: visualizes the cumulative contribution of each pipeline step and explains the science-domain exception.
Figure 6: twelve-panel benchmark-level expansion of the headline, including held-out tasks.
Table 2 plus Tables 31–33: connects source quality to the full long-tail candidate set.
Figure 11 and Figure 12: complementary instability/average views for AIW generalization.
failure_patterns: Dense appendix grids and long tables compress labels, series and standard-error subscripts below comfortable reading size.
Color-heavy categorical charts often lack complete grayscale redundancy, especially when many trajectories overlap.
Several captions state findings but omit replicate counts or uncertainty definitions; Figure 11 calls bars “variance” without specifying the plotted statistic.
Prompt screenshots publish interface text but not prompt version, model, sampling settings or source-file provenance.
Figure 6 held-out status is described in prose/caption but not marked as a visual grouping, and the reading inventory under-counted its PDF panels (nine vs twelve).
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: OpenThoughts uses a saturated, baseline-anchored scaling grammar to turn a sequential data-curation recipe into cumulative, benchmark-level and robustness evidence, then publishes the hidden prompt interfaces and full ablation tables in a deliberately dense appendix.
